title: Type Checking with basedpyright
text: This guide covers how to configure basedpyright for a ROS 2 workspace managed with pixi. basedpyright is a stricter fork of pyright with better defaults and improved error messages.

title: Type Checking with basedpyright
text:
Why basedpyright
Standard pyright works fine for general Python, but ROS 2 introduces friction:

rclpy, px4_msgs, and most ROS packages ship no type stubs.
Generated message classes have loose constructors that trigger false-positive argument-type errors.
The install tree lives in install/ (a colcon artifact), not in the standard site-packages location.

basedpyright provides more granular per-rule configuration so you can silence ROS-specific false positives while still catching real errors in your own code.

title: Type Checking with basedpyright
text:
Installation

Inside the pixi environment (recommended)
Add basedpyright to a dev feature so it is not bundled into production builds:
# pixi.toml
[feature.dev.pypi-dependencies]
basedpyright = "*"

[environments]
dev = { features = ["dev"], solve-group = "default" }
Install and run:
pixi install -e dev
pixi run -e dev basedpyright src/


Global install (for the LSP / editor)
# via pip
pip install basedpyright

# via npm (also installs the language server)
npm install -g basedpyright
The VSCode extension is basedpyright (detachhead.basedpyright). Do not mix an npm install with the VSCode extension – let the extension manage its own binary.

title: Type Checking with basedpyright
text:
pyrightconfig.json
Place pyrightconfig.json at the workspace root (same directory as pixi.toml).
{
  "typeCheckingMode": "basic",
  "pythonVersion": "3.11",
  "pythonPlatform": "Linux",

  "include": ["src"],
  "exclude": [
    "**/node_modules",
    "**/__pycache__",
    "**/.*",
    "build",
    "install",
    "log"
  ],

  "reportMissingImports": true,
  "reportMissingTypeStubs": false,

  "reportUnusedImport": true,
  "reportUnusedVariable": true,

  "reportGeneralTypeIssues": true,
  "reportOptionalMemberAccess": true,
  "reportOptionalSubscript": true,
  "reportOptionalOperand": true,
  "reportOptionalIterable": true,
  "reportOptionalContextManager": true,
  "reportOptionalCallOperand": true,

  "reportArgumentType": false
}

Settings explained








Setting
Value
Reason




typeCheckingMode
"basic"
Avoids false positives from untyped ROS packages. Upgrade to "standard" once stubs improve.


pythonVersion
"3.11"
Must match the Python version in pixi.toml.


include
["src"]
Only analyse your packages; ignore colcon build artefacts.


exclude
build, install, log
Colcon output contains generated C-extension stubs that confuse the checker.


reportMissingTypeStubs
false
rclpy, px4_msgs, and most ROS packages have no .pyi stubs.


reportArgumentType
false
Generated message classes have loose __init__ signatures that produce spurious errors.

title: Type Checking with basedpyright
section: Pointing basedpyright at the pixi environment
text:
Pointing basedpyright at the pixi environment
basedpyright must resolve imports from the pixi environment, not system Python.

Option A – venvPath (recommended)
{
  "venvPath": ".",
  "venv": ".pixi/envs/default"
}
This tells basedpyright to look for the virtual environment at .pixi/envs/default relative to the project root.


Option B – pythonPath
{
  "pythonPath": ".pixi/envs/default/bin/python"
}
Use this if venvPath does not correctly resolve stubs.






Tip



Verify interpreter resolution:
basedpyright --outputjson src/ 2>&1 | python -m json.tool | grep pythonPath

title: Type Checking with basedpyright
text:
ROS 2-specific notes

rclpy stubs
rclpy has partial stubs on PyPI. They are often outdated but reduce reportMissingTypeStubs noise:
[feature.dev.pypi-dependencies]
rclpy-stubs = "*"
Alternatively, generate stubs from the installed package:
# inside pixi shell
stubgen -p rclpy -o typestubs/
Then register the stub path in pyrightconfig.json:
{
  "stubPath": "typestubs"
}


px4_msgs
px4_msgs is a C extension built by colcon. After building, point basedpyright to its install location:
{
  "extraPaths": [
    "install/px4_msgs/lib/python3.11/site-packages"
  ]
}
If you used venvPath above and the pixi activation already sourced install/setup.bash, this may not be necessary.


Launch files
ROS 2 launch files (.launch.py) use dynamic LaunchArgument substitutions that cannot be statically analysed. Suppress errors per-file:
# pyright: reportGeneralTypeIssues=false

title: Type Checking with basedpyright
text:
VSCode integration
Add to .vscode/settings.json:
{
  "python.defaultInterpreterPath":
      "${workspaceFolder}/.pixi/envs/default/bin/python",

  "basedpyright.pythonPath":
      "${workspaceFolder}/.pixi/envs/default/bin/python",

  "basedpyright.disableOrganizeImports": false
}
python.defaultInterpreterPath ensures the VSCode Python extension, IntelliSense, and basedpyright all share the same pixi interpreter.

title: Type Checking with basedpyright
text:
Running from the CLI
# Check all packages under src/
pixi run -e dev basedpyright src/

# Check a single package
pixi run -e dev basedpyright src/my_package/

# JSON output for CI
pixi run -e dev basedpyright --outputjson src/ > typecheck.json

title: Type Checking with basedpyright
text:
Incrementally tightening type checking
Start at "basic" to suppress ROS-stub noise. Tighten per-package as you add type annotations or as upstream stubs improve.
basic  ->  standard  ->  strict  ->  all
To apply stricter checking to a specific file, add a comment at the top:
# pyright: standard
To apply it to an entire subtree, add a nested pyrightconfig.json in that subdirectory with only the overridden key:
{
  "typeCheckingMode": "standard"
}
The root pyrightconfig.json still governs everything else.

title: Frame Conventions
text: PX4 and ROS 2 use different coordinate frames. Every quantity exchanged over uXRCE-DDS must be converted at the boundary. This page defines the frames, the conversion rules, and the C++ implementations used in uav_control.

title: Workspace Setup
text: This guide covers how to set up a self-contained ROS 2 (Jazzy) workspace targeting PX4 SITL using pixi as the environment and package manager.

title: Workspace Setup
text:
Project structure
my_ros2_ws/
+-- src/
|   +-- my_package/             # your ROS 2 packages
|   +-- px4_msgs/               # git submodule (PX4 message definitions)
+-- pixi.toml                   # environment + task definitions
+-- pixi.lock                   # committed; pins all resolved versions
+-- activate.sh                 # sources install/setup.bash on shell entry
+-- pyrightconfig.json          # basedpyright config (see Type Checking)
+-- install/                    # colcon output     (gitignored)
+-- build/                      # colcon build tree (gitignored)
+-- log/                        # colcon logs       (gitignored)

title: Workspace Setup
text:
pixi.toml

Workspace metadata
[workspace]
name     = "my_ros2_ws"
version  = "0.1.0"
channels = ["robostack-jazzy", "conda-forge"]
platforms = ["linux-64"]






Warning



Channel order matters. robostack-jazzy must come before conda-forge. Reversing the order causes the solver to pick incompatible libstdc++ builds and break ROS package resolution.




Dependencies
[dependencies]
# --- ROS 2 Jazzy ---
ros-jazzy-ros-base             = "*"
ros-jazzy-ament-cmake          = "*"
ros-jazzy-rclcpp               = "*"
ros-jazzy-std-msgs             = "*"
ros-jazzy-geometry-msgs        = "*"
ros-jazzy-sensor-msgs          = "*"
ros-jazzy-nav-msgs             = "*"
ros-jazzy-tf2                  = "*"
ros-jazzy-tf2-ros              = "*"
ros-jazzy-tf2-geometry-msgs    = "*"
ros-jazzy-ros2launch           = "*"
ros-jazzy-launch-ros           = "*"
ros-jazzy-rosbag2              = "*"
ros-jazzy-rosbag2-storage-mcap = "*"
ros-jazzy-plotjuggler-ros      = "*"

# --- Build tooling ---
colcon-common-extensions = "*"
cmake                    = "*"
ninja                    = "*"
compilers                = "*"

# --- C++ libraries ---
eigen    = "*"
yaml-cpp = "*"

# --- Python ---
python     = ">=3.11"
numpy      = "*"
scipy      = "*"
matplotlib = "*"






Note



GPU-accelerated nodes (optional): add cuda-toolkit = ">=12.0,<13" under [dependencies] if your workspace includes CUDA nodes. The host driver must already be installed (nvidia-smi should report >= 525 for CUDA 12).




PyPI-only packages
For packages not on conda channels, use [pypi-dependencies]:
[pypi-dependencies]
scienceplots = "*"


Activation script
[activation]
scripts = ["activate.sh"]

title: Workspace Setup
text:
Workspace activation
Every time pixi launches a shell or runs a task it sources the scripts listed under [activation]. Use this to overlay the colcon install tree.
activate.sh (project root):
INSTALL_DIR="${PIXI_PROJECT_ROOT}/install"

if [ -f "${INSTALL_DIR}/setup.bash" ]; then
  source "${INSTALL_DIR}/setup.bash"
fi
PIXI_PROJECT_ROOT is set automatically to the directory containing pixi.toml. The if guard prevents errors on a clean checkout before the first build.

title: Workspace Setup
text:
PX4 message definitions (submodule)
px4_msgs must be built with colcon as a standard ROS 2 package. It is tracked as a git submodule so that the version is pinned to the exact PX4 firmware release you are flying against.

Adding the submodule
git submodule add -b release/1.16 \
    https://github.com/PX4/px4_msgs.git src/px4_msgs


Restoring on a fresh clone
git clone --recurse-submodules <repo-url>
# or, after a plain clone:
git submodule update --init --recursive


.gitmodules entry
[submodule "src/px4_msgs"]
    path   = src/px4_msgs
    url    = https://github.com/PX4/px4_msgs.git
    branch = release/1.16






Warning



Always pin px4_msgs to the same release branch as the PX4 firmware used for SITL (release/1.14, release/1.15, release/1.16, …). A mismatch produces silent serialization errors: topics publish but subscribers receive garbage.




Versioned topic names
From PX4 v1.14 onward, some topics are published under a versioned name to signal a breaking message-definition change. The most common case is VehicleStatus, which moved from:
/fmu/out/vehicle_status      # pre-v1.14
/fmu/out/vehicle_status_v1   # v1.14+
If your subscriber listens on the wrong topic name it receives no data at all — the subscription simply never fires. Auto-arming logic that waits for arming_state == ARMING_STATE_ARMED blocks forever, and the vehicle never arms.
The fix is to subscribe to the versioned topic:
// px4_interface.cpp / px4_manager_node.cpp
status_sub_ = node_->create_subscription<px4_msgs::msg::VehicleStatus>(
    "/fmu/out/vehicle_status_v1", qos, callback);
Check which topics are actually being published by the running firmware:
ros2 topic list | grep vehicle_status
Use whichever name appears — it tells you exactly what the firmware is advertising.


Diagnosing version mismatches
If the topic name is correct but arming still fails, the submodule and firmware are on different releases (fields added/removed between releases cause silent deserialization errors). Check alignment:
# commit that your workspace px4_msgs is pinned to
git -C src/px4_msgs rev-parse HEAD

# PX4 version string printed at SITL startup, e.g. "PX4 v1.15.2"
# must correspond to the same release branch
To fix, update the submodule to the branch matching your firmware:
cd src/px4_msgs
git fetch
git checkout release/1.16   # match PX4 firmware version
cd ../..
colcon build --symlink-install
git add src/px4_msgs
git commit -m "chore: pin px4_msgs to release/1.16"

title: Workspace Setup
text:
Build tasks
Define all build and launch operations as pixi tasks. Every task runs inside the activated environment, so ros2, colcon, cmake, and nvcc are all on PATH.
[tasks]
# Build all packages with symlink install and compile commands export
build = "colcon build --symlink-install --cmake-args -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=1"

# Remove all colcon output
clean = "rm -rf build install log"

# Run all tests with live console output
test = "colcon test --event-handlers console_direct+"

# Launch control nodes only (PX4 running externally)
launch = { cmd = "ros2 launch my_bringup sitl.launch.py",
           depends-on = ["build"] }

# Full SITL stack: PX4 + micro-XRCE-DDS agent + control nodes
px4-sitl = { cmd = "ros2 launch my_bringup px4_sitl.launch.py \
                     launch_px4:=true launch_agent:=true record_bag:=false",
             depends-on = ["build"] }

# Canned trajectories
hover = { cmd = "ros2 launch my_bringup px4_sitl.launch.py \
                 launch_px4:=true launch_agent:=true \
                 trajectory_type:=hover z:=2.0 duration:=90.0",
          depends-on = ["build"] }

lemniscate = { cmd = "ros2 launch my_bringup px4_sitl.launch.py \
                      launch_px4:=true launch_agent:=true \
                      trajectory_type:=lemniscate A:=3.0 omega:=0.2 z:=2.0",
               depends-on = ["build"] }

circular = { cmd = "ros2 launch my_bringup px4_sitl.launch.py \
                    launch_px4:=true launch_agent:=true \
                    trajectory_type:=circular A:=3.0 omega:=0.2 z:=2.0",
             depends-on = ["build"] }
Run any task with:
pixi run build
pixi run px4-sitl
pixi run hover
The depends-on field guarantees the workspace is rebuilt before launching.

title: Workspace Setup
text:
Daily workflow
# After adding or updating packages in pixi.toml
pixi install

# Build all ROS 2 packages
pixi run build

# Run tests
pixi run test

# Interactive shell with the full environment active
pixi shell

# Clean rebuild
pixi run clean
pixi run build

title: Workspace Setup
text:
Troubleshooting

package 'xxx' not found after adding a new ROS package
The colcon install overlay is stale. Run pixi run build.


ros2: command not found inside pixi shell
The activation script did not run. Verify:

activate.sh exists at the project root.
pixi.toml contains [activation] scripts = ["activate.sh"].
You entered the environment with pixi shell or pixi run <task>.



CUDA compiler (nvcc) not found
Only needed if your workspace has GPU-accelerated nodes.

Add cuda-toolkit = ">=12.0,<13" to [dependencies] in pixi.toml.
Run pixi install to fetch it.
Inside pixi shell, which nvcc should resolve to .pixi/envs/default/bin/nvcc.



colcon picks up system Python instead of pixi Python
pixi prepends its environment to PATH, but a stale shell may still resolve system Python. Exit and re-enter with pixi shell.


pixi.lock conflicts on git pull
pixi.lock is a committed file. If it conflicts, accept the incoming version and run pixi install to re-sync your local environment.

title: Low-Level Offboard Control
text:
Low-level offboard control means bypassing PX4’s position/velocity controllers and sending commands directly to the inner loops. Three levels are available, selected at runtime via a ROS 2 parameter:
Reference implementation: SaxionMechatronics/px4_offboard_lowlevel.

title: Low-Level Offboard Control
Low-Level Offboard Control
text:
Frame conventions
PX4 uses NED / FRD (North-East-Down, Front-Right-Down). ROS and most controllers use ENU / FLU (East-North-Up, Front-Left-Up). All setpoints must be converted before publishing, and all odometry must be converted after reading.
See Frame Conventions for the full conversion reference including vector permutations, quaternion transforms, altitude sign, and yaw convention.

title: Low-Level Offboard Control
Low-Level Offboard Control
Low-Level Offboard Control
Low-Level Offboard Control
text:
Control allocation (wrench -> throttles)
To produce per-motor throttles from a desired wrench [tau_x, tau_y, tau_z, T]:
\[
\boldsymbol{\omega} = \mathbf{M}^+ \mathbf{w}, \quad
\text{PWM}_i = c_2 \omega_i^2 + c_1 \omega_i + c_0, \quad
\delta_i = \frac{\text{PWM}_i - \text{PWM}_\text{min}}{\text{PWM}_\text{max} - \text{PWM}_\text{min}}
\]
where \(\mathbf{M}\) is the control allocation matrix (arm geometry + motor constants) and \(\mathbf{M}^+\) is its pseudoinverse.
For a symmetric X-quadrotor with arm length \(l\) and thrust/moment constants \(k_T\), \(k_M\):
\[
\mathbf{M} = \begin{pmatrix}
-k_T l \sin 45^\circ & k_T l \sin 45^\circ & k_T l \sin 45^\circ & -k_T l \sin 45^\circ \\
-k_T l \sin 45^\circ & k_T l \sin 45^\circ & -k_T l \sin 45^\circ & k_T l \sin 45^\circ \\
-k_M k_T & -k_M k_T & k_M k_T & k_M k_T \\
k_T & k_T & k_T & k_T
\end{pmatrix}
\]
SITL skips the PWM conversion and maps throttles directly via SIM_GZ_EC_MIN / SIM_GZ_EC_MAX (rotor speed limits in rad/s).

x500 parameters (reference)
uav_parameters:
  mass: 2.064              # kg
  arm_length: 0.25         # m
  num_of_arms: 4
  inertia: {x: 0.08612, y: 0.08962, z: 0.16088}   # kg.m^2
  thrust_constant: 8.54858e-06   # N.s^2/rad^2
  moment_constant: 0.016         # m
  max_rotor_speed: 1000          # rad/s
  gravity: 9.81
  omega_to_pwm_coefficient: {x_2: 0.001142, x_1: 0.2273, x_0: 914.2}
  PWM_MIN: 1075
  PWM_MAX: 1950
  SIM_GZ_EC_MAX: 1000    # rad/s
  SIM_GZ_EC_MIN: 150     # rad/s

title: Low-Level Offboard Control
text:
Switching modes at runtime
The control mode can be changed without restarting the node:
ros2 param set /offboard_controller control_mode 2   # -> thrust + torque
ros2 param set /offboard_controller control_mode 3   # -> direct actuator
ros2 param set /offboard_controller control_mode 1   # -> attitude (default)
The OffboardControlMode heartbeat automatically switches its active field on the next publish cycle.

title: C++ Tooling with clangd
text: This guide covers the .clangd configuration used across uav_control and related ROS 2 C++ packages. The setup gives accurate clangd completions and clang-tidy diagnostics inside a colcon workspace without false positives from GPU or ROS-specific compiler flags.

title: C++ Tooling with clangd
text:
How clangd finds headers
clangd reads compile_commands.json to know which flags were used to build each translation unit. colcon generates this file at the workspace root when you pass --cmake-args -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON:
colcon build --cmake-args -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON
The .clangd file then tells clangd where to look:
CompileFlags:
    CompilationDatabase: "."
"." resolves to the directory containing .clangd, which should be the workspace root (the directory that contains src/, build/, install/).

title: C++ Tooling with clangd
text:
Base configuration
CompileFlags:
    CompilationDatabase: "."
    Add: ["-std=c++17", "-Wno-unknown-argument"]
    Remove:
        [
            "--generate-code=*",
            "--options-file",
            "--options-file=*",
            "-rdc=*",
            "-forward-unknown-to-host-compiler",
            "-Xcompiler=*",
            "--expt-relaxed-constexpr",
        ]
The Remove list strips NVCC-specific flags that clang does not understand. Without this, clangd crashes or emits spurious errors on any package that links against CUDA.
-Wno-unknown-argument suppresses the resulting unknown-flag warnings for any flags not caught by the Remove list.

title: C++ Tooling with clangd
text:
clang-tidy checks
The project runs the full clang-tidy suite (Add: ["*"]) with a focused suppress list. The suppressed checks fall into two categories:
Style preferences — rules that conflict with the project’s conventions:







Check
Reason suppressed




google-build-*, google-readability-*
Google style not used


modernize-use-trailing-return-type
Trailing return types add noise for simple functions


modernize-use-nodiscard
Overly noisy for internal helpers


readability-identifier-length
Short names (e.g. dt, u) are idiomatic in control code


readability-magic-numbers, cppcoreguidelines-avoid-magic-numbers
Physical constants and gains are fine inline


readability-function-cognitive-complexity
MPPI kernels are inherently long



False positives in ROS 2 / robotics code:







Check
Reason suppressed




cppcoreguidelines-avoid-non-const-global-variables
ROS node handles and parameter servers are globals by convention


cppcoreguidelines-pro-type-vararg
Some ROS logging macros use varargs


cppcoreguidelines-pro-bounds-array-to-pointer-decay
Common in Eigen / low-level math


cppcoreguidelines-special-member-functions, hicpp-special-member-functions
Rule-of-five is not required for RAII wrappers with shared_ptr


misc-non-private-member-variables-in-classes, cppcoreguidelines-non-private-member-variables-in-classes
Parameter structs use public fields intentionally


cppcoreguidelines-prefer-member-initializer
Conflicts with complex constructor delegation patterns


misc-include-cleaner
Generates excessive noise from transitively included ROS headers



Vendor-specific suites (llvmlibc-*, fuchsia-*, altera-*) are suppressed wholesale as they target entirely different platforms.

title: C++ Tooling with clangd
text:
CUDA file handling
.cu files need special treatment because compile_commands.json records the NVCC invocation, not a clang-compatible command. A conditional block remaps them to clang with CUDA-host-only parsing:
---
If:
    PathMatch: ".*\\.cu$"
CompileFlags:
    Compiler: clang++
    Add:
        [
            "-xcuda",
            "--cuda-host-only",
            "--cuda-path=/usr/local/cuda",
            "--cuda-gpu-arch=sm_75",
            "-Wno-unknown-cuda-version",
            "-ferror-limit=0",
        ]
    Remove:
        [
            "/usr/local/cuda-*/bin/nvcc",
            "--generate-code=*",
            "--options-file",
            "--options-file=*",
            "-rdc=*",
            "-forward-unknown-to-host-compiler",
            "-Xcompiler=*",
            "--expt-relaxed-constexpr",
            "-x", "cu", "cuda",
        ]
Diagnostics:
    Suppress:
        - "cuda_ovl_target"
        - "redefinition"
        - "constexpr_redecl_mismatch"
        - "variadic_device_fn"
        - "attributes_not_allowed"
        - "undeclared_var_use"
--cuda-host-only tells clang to only parse host code, which avoids the need for a full CUDA device compiler toolchain. The Suppress list silences redefinition errors that arise from CUDA’s dual-compilation model.
Adjust --cuda-gpu-arch to match your GPU (e.g. sm_86 for Ampere, sm_89 for Ada Lovelace).

title: C++ Tooling with clangd
text:
Placement
Put .clangd at the workspace root (the directory that contains src/), not inside individual packages. clangd searches upward from the open file to find the nearest .clangd, so a single workspace-root file covers all packages.
my_ws/
  .clangd            <-- here
  compile_commands.json
  src/
    uav_control/
    px4_msgs/

title: C++ Tooling with clangd
text:
Troubleshooting

clangd cannot find compile_commands.json
Run a full build with compile commands export enabled:
colcon build --cmake-args -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON
Then confirm the file exists at the workspace root:
ls compile_commands.json


False-positive #include errors after adding a new package
colcon build must be re-run so the new package’s headers appear in compile_commands.json. clangd will re-index automatically once the file is updated.


clangd crashes on .cu files
Confirm clang++ is on PATH inside the pixi environment:
pixi run which clang++
If missing, add clangxx (or clang) to [dependencies] in pixi.toml.
